diagnostic_evidence.quote: \item[(b)] (\textit{Trust-region not used}) \,\,  $r_{n}\equiv \infty$ and the majorization gap $h_{n}^{(i)}$ satisfies the quadratic lower bound

issues.failure_explanation: The stated upper bound for case A3(a) contains the constant ρ (appearing in L/ρ), but ρ is only defined in A3(b) (as the constant in the quadratic lower bound on the majorization gap). Under A3(a) alone, ρ is undefined, making the bound ill-defined. The proof actually yields the finite bound (L/2)Σr_n² + (f(θ_0)−f*) + 2mΣΔ_n without any ρ dependence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the stated A3(a) bound with the bound obtained in the proof: (L/2)Σr_n² + (f(θ_0)−f*) + 2mΣΔ_n < ∞, removing the undefined ρ dependence.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit bound stated in Proposition 3 for the A3(a) case is ill-defined. The finiteness conclusion remains correct (the proof supplies a valid bound without ρ), and downstream constants M_1 in Theorem 1 are unaffected.
issues.title: Proposition 3 bound for case A3(a) references undefined constant ρ
issues.why_classification: The corrected bound is directly available from the proof, is local, and preserves every substantive claim and guarantee. No new lemma or argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the majorization gap $h_{n}^{(i)}$ satisfies the quadratic lower bound $h_{n}^{(i)}(\theta) \ge \frac{\rho}{2}\lVert \theta - \theta_{n-1}^{(i)} \rVert^{2}$ \textup{for all $\theta\in \Theta^{(i)}$}

\item[(b)] (\textit{Trust-region not used}) \,\,  If $r_{n}\equiv \infty$, then surrogates  $g_{n}^{(i)}$ for all $n,i$ have $L_{g}$-Lipschitz contiuous gradients  for some constant $L_{g}>0$ and are $\lambda$-strongly convex  for some constant $\lambda>0$

issues.failure_explanation: A3(b) assumes only that the majorization gap h_n^{(i)} satisfies a quadratic lower bound at θ_{n−1}^{(i)}. This does not imply that the surrogate g_n^{(i)} is λ-strongly convex. Strong convexity of g is assumed in A5(b), not A3(b). Without strong convexity of g, the key inequality (λ/2)‖θ_n − θ_n*‖² ≤ Δ_n need not hold: when g is convex but flat near its minimizer set (e.g., g(θ) = (θ²−1)⁺ with minimizer set [−1,1]), one can have Δ_n = 0 while ‖θ_n − θ_n*‖ = 2 for distinct minimizers. The proposition is stated under A1–A4 only and is therefore false in general under A3(b).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that g_n^{(i)} is λ-strongly convex (as in A5(b)) to the statement of Proposition 4 for the A3(b) case, or restrict Proposition 4's A3(b) case to the setting where A5(b) is assumed. This is a local hypothesis addition that leaves Theorem 1 and all downstream results intact.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 4's conclusion ‖θ_n^{(i)} − θ_n^{(i*)}‖ = o(1) is not established under A1–A4 with A3(b) alone. The proof of Theorem 1(iii) under A3(b) relies on Proposition 4, but Theorem 1(iii) additionally assumes A5 (which supplies strong convexity), so the main theorem survives if the proposition is restated with A5(b).
issues.title: Proposition 4 proof uses strong convexity of g not implied by A3(b)
issues.why_classification: The formal statement of Proposition 4 is false as written and its proof uses an assumption not present in its hypotheses. The repair requires adding a nontrivial hypothesis (strong convexity of g) but is a contained fix: the main theorem already assumes this hypothesis where the result is used. No new proof architecture or major loss results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Points \ref{NMF_claim_1}-\ref{NMF_claim_2} verify that \eqref{eq:MUPR_NMF} is a particular instance of BMM (Alg. \ref{algorithm:BMM-DR}).

issues.failure_explanation: The BMM framework (eq:EBMM) requires sequential (Gauss-Seidel) block updates: the i-th block update uses the already-updated values θ_n^{(1)},…,θ_n^{(i−1)} of earlier blocks. In MUR (eq:MUPR_NMF), the H-update produces H_{n+1}, but the subsequent W-update uses the stale H_n rather than the freshly computed H_{n+1}. Thus the W-update surrogate majorizes f(W,H_n) instead of the BMM block objective f(H_{n+1},W), making MUR a simultaneous (Jacobi) update rather than a BMM (Gauss-Seidel) update. This is confirmed by noting that setting δ = ρ = 0 recovers the standard MU of Lee–Seung, which is likewise a simultaneous update.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the W-update in eq:MUPR_NMF to use H_{n+1} instead of H_n (i.e., W_{n+1}^T ← W_n^T ⊙ (H_{n+1}X^T + ρW̃_n^T) ⊘ ((H_{n+1}H_{n+1}^T + ρI)W̃_n^T)), making MUR a sequential BMM update. This preserves all convergence and complexity claims for the modified algorithm, but the modified MUR no longer reduces to standard MU when δ = ρ = 0 and the numerical experiments as conducted do not validate the modified algorithm.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary 1 (cor:NMF) is invalid because the proof applies Theorem 1 to MUR, which does not satisfy the BMM framework. The MUR option (f) in Corollary cor:NTF (cor:NTF) is likewise affected. The convergence and complexity guarantees claimed for MUR as stated are unsupported.
issues.title: MUR algorithm is not a BMM instance: W-update uses stale H instead of updated H
issues.why_classification: A one-index change repairs the BMM structure and restores all mathematical guarantees. The modified algorithm is recognizably comparable (a sequential BMM version of the multiplicative update). However, the repair necessarily changes the algorithm's iterates and loses the claimed reduction to MU, so it is more than minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, the sub-level sets $f^{-1}((-\infty, a])=\{ \param\in \Param\,:\, f(\param)\le a \}$ for $a\in \R$ are compact.

issues.failure_explanation: The NMF objective f(W,H) = (1/2)‖X−WH‖²_F is invariant under the scaling (W,H) → (cW, H/c) for any c > 0. For any (W,H) in a sub-level set {(W,H) : f(W,H) ≤ a}, the scaled point (cW, H/c) has the same objective value and lies in the same sub-level set. As c → ∞ the scaled point diverges in the parameter space, so every sub-level set is unbounded and hence non-compact. The same scaling invariance applies to the NCPD objective ‖X − Σ_k ⊗U^{(i)}[:,k]‖²_F (scaling one factor up and another down). Thus A2 fails for both NMF and NCPD with the stated unbounded constraint sets Θ = R_{≥0}^{p×r} × R_{≥0}^{r×N}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair preserving the advertised unbounded-constraint regime is identified; at minimum, a repair must either (i) restrict the constraint sets Θ^{(i)} to compact convex sets so that A2 holds and Theorem 1 applies (losing the unbounded nonnegativity setting central to NMF/NCPD), or (ii) establish boundedness of the MUR/BMM-DR iterates by a new argument exploiting the thresholding δ > 0 and proximal regularization ρ > 0, which would require a nontrivial lemma not present in the source.
issues.overall_effect: The compact sub-level sets condition in A2 is essential for Proposition 2 (boundedness of iterates), which in turn underpins the Lipschitz-constant estimates and all subsequent rate and complexity bounds. Without A2, the iterates need not be bounded, and Theorem 1 cannot be applied. Corollary 1 (cor:NMF) and Corollary cor:NTF (cor:NTF) are therefore invalid for the stated unbounded nonnegativity constraints, which constitute the paper's principal applications.
issues.title: Assumption A2 (compact sub-level sets) fails for NMF and NCPD due to scaling invariance
issues.why_classification: Every source-supported resolution either excludes the advertised unbounded-constraint regime for NMF/NCPD (a major loss of the paper's main application) or requires essentially new proof architecture to establish iterate boundedness without compact sub-level sets. No comparable version of the primary claim (complexity and convergence for NMF/NCPD with standard nonnegativity constraints) survives under any source-supported repair.
